summary: The revised receipt resolved all five comparisons, and resolving them caught a real error in what I recorded last turn, so this update is a correction rather than an extension. The lease still failed to suppress the transfer-marked request: the incumbent leader adopted term 3 and became a follower, which is the violated comparison on its own event (index 69 of CheckRun 026b6c86522d454299d1f3ca358c009e, StateFollower at term 3 where it had been StateLeader at term 2) and is the actual cost of the bypass, since without the marker the same request would have been dropped by the lease as ordinary election traffic is. But it did not grant the vote — it rejected it (index 67, responded true, granted false), because the candidate advertised last entry (index 10, term 1) while the incumbent held (index 11, term 2), so isUpToDate failed and the module's own log records the rejection. My previous rationale said the incumbent voted for its own replacement and became a follower in its wake; the events never supported that, and I had read a responded flag as a grant. The corrected wiring is precisely what made it visible, since the incumbent-vote comparison now resolves as holding, and the campaign won anyway on the triggering follower's own vote plus the third voter's grant (index 68, StateLeader at term 3). So the finding is narrower and sharper than I wrote: the lease does not stop a peer claiming the leader's authority from making a healthy incumbent abandon its term and its leadership, and the incumbent's ballot is not the harm — its term and its leadership are. The judgment is unchanged, since the trigger still requires a non-leader to send MsgTimeoutNow and no snapshot statement asks a receiver to check the sender against its own r.lead. I also recorded a harness fact that matters for reading every election in this run: in this fixture the followers never hold the leader's uncommitted term-2 entry at index 11, so the incumbent is ahead of every other voter and a candidate drawn from the followers can never win its ballot — which is why that vote is a rejection here and was simply not needed in the earlier forged-election receipts. The update keeps both receipts, with the older one cited only for the setup, control and trigger events it records unambiguously and a joint-history note explaining that it and the revision are the same fixture with different wiring; it also keeps the marker knowledge use, now asserting that the marker's effect landed on the incumbent as a term change and a demotion rather than as a granted vote. Submission validates with execution_requested=false and nothing uncited.
